critical-bundle-gzip.reason:
SPEC §21.1: 516 KB gzip against the 350 KB budget, 355 KB of it mb_bg.wasm. The WASM doubled between M0 and M7 and mb-crdt's yrs is the suspect; the JS has grown with the M7 shell. Untried levers: opt-level s/z for the wasm build, wasm-opt -Oz, and splitting mb-crdt out of the initial chunk. Compression is the bigger win and comes first — the server sends this uncompressed today. Carried, not ignored: this harness exists so §21.3's measure-before-and-after can be satisfied before anyone touches opt-level. Tolerance is 0% for bytes, so any growth from here fails the build.

Raised by 1,399 bytes (526,850 → 528,249) for the inline task view: the node view in web/src/editor/task-view.ts, its chip helpers, and the CSS for both. That is §10.2 — a checkbox and metadata chips — which the application shipped without through M7, so this is a required feature and not an optional one, and 1.4 KB is proportionate to it. It is measured rather than estimated, and it changes none of the reasoning above: the 355 KB of WASM is still where the budget is lost and still where the fix is. Re-measure this line after compression lands rather than trimming a kilobyte of feature code for it.

keystroke-to-paint.reason: A measurement limit rather than a regression, and recorded rather than waved away. The figure is a double-requestAnimationFrame from the keydown, so it includes the wait for the next vsync boundary: 16.4 ms is one 60 Hz frame, which is the answer 'the keystroke made the next frame' rounded up to the frame it made. The technique cannot resolve better than that, and Event Timing — which could — is quantised to 8 ms by Chromium and so cannot either. What it does still catch is the failure the budget exists for: a keystroke costing two or three frames. Removing this entry needs a sub-frame technique, not a faster keystroke. SPEC §21.4.

longest-task.reason: A real finding, on the throttled mobile profile only: the longest main-thread task during a cold start is 65 ms against a 50 ms budget, and it is in bootstrap — instantiating a 945 KB WASM module and mounting the editor. Same root cause as the bundle breach above, so the same fix order applies and this number should be re-measured after it. Desktop is inside budget and is deliberately not recorded here, so a desktop regression still fails the build.
